author: independent critic pair acting as one reviewer for the education and SME roles (did not author the bank or the blueprint), 2026-11-19; read all 30 items, the blueprint, the 18 taught artifact.html pages, the topic artifact.gift banks, checkpoint-mcq.gift and the authoring notes; keys judged from the taught pages and prior knowledge of the Docker, Compose, GitHub Actions, FastAPI and Spring docs, official docs not re-fetched and no key executed in this session; targeted course-final-gift test passes (32/32); one pass, no recheck, no reconciliation

findings.claim: The key needs two facts that no taught page states: that ghcr.io is GitHub's own registry and that GITHUB_TOKEN with a packages permission can push to it. secrets-in-ci teaches only that every run gets a GITHUB_TOKEN restricted by a permissions block and that a fork run receives it; the jenkins-registries page uses ghcr.io only as an example registry in an image reference and never mentions credentials. A learner who knows only the course cannot tell the key (GITHUB_TOKEN for ghcr.io) from D (a stored secret for both registries). The item is tagged jenkins-registries-cd-and-kubernetes#o2 (read an image reference) and secrets-in-ci#o3, and neither objective covers registry login. This is out of taught scope in a graded final.
findings.recommendation: Either rework so the stem supplies the missing fact (for example state that GHCR accepts the run's GITHUB_TOKEN when the job's permissions include packages: write) or replace the item with one decided by taught content, such as secrets-in-ci#o3 on the permissions block alone.

findings.claim: These easy items re-ask facts that the topic practice banks already decide: q01 combines 'reuse a name' and 'effect of --rm' (containers-and-images), q03 inverts 'same images' and 'Podman on macOS', and q08 asks the /usr/share/nginx/html path that multi-stage-builds 'o2 front-end copy' asks. Each is a fresh scenario, not a copy, but a learner who did the topic quizzes gets them as recall.
findings.recommendation: Accept as breadth items or lift one scenario step each; no change is needed for validity.

location.selector: q22 option C, q30 options A and D

findings.claim: Weak distractors. q22 C ('down -v would have kept the edit in a volume') is a counterfactual that contradicts itself. q30 A ('Compose rebuilt the image, so the edit was not saved') contradicts the stem, which says the old behaviour remains. q30 D (a bind mount that refreshes only on stop) is implausible for a service the stem says is built. Each works as an elimination giveaway.
findings.recommendation: Replace with plausible misconceptions, for example for q30 'up -d rebuilds only when the Dockerfile changes' or 'the container needs docker compose restart api first'.

findings.claim: The key rests on 'each job runs on its own runner', which the pipeline page states only in passing ('jobs, each on a runner'). Passing files between jobs, artifacts and caches are not taught. Defensible for a hard item, but it is the least-taught step in the bank.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add 'a new runner for each job' to the stem or accept; no key change.
